text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The coalition parties Wednesday proposed that the Tocsik commission be dissolved.

- Defense Minister Gyorgy Keleti, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs and Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze recently met informally to discuss the Operation Birch Tree scandal that is proving ever more inconvenient to the government.
- The cabinet is expected to decide today on the date of the next elections.
- Senior Free Democrat politicians yesterday denied that the party was considering leaving the coalition, as reported in Nepszabadsag.

- In its inquiry into the sale of Budapest Bank the State Audit Office (ASZ) is asking the government to examine the role of former Finance Minister Lajos Bokros, Finance Ministry state secretary Tibor Draskovics and former deputy state secretary Eva Hegedus.
- A Polish-Czech-Hungarian prime ministerial meeting will be held in Cracow on August 22 to discuss issues related to NATO membership and accession to the European Union.
- US Defense Secretary William Cohen will visit Hungary after the July 8 NATO summit in Madrid.

- Both GDP growth and inflation exceeded expectations in the first half year, increasing the likelihood that the government's economic targets will be reached, National Bank president Gyorgy Suranyi told a news conference.
- Labor Minister Peter Kiss told a press conference yesterday that the present unemployment rate is, calculated by the norms of the European Union, 9.2%, lower than the 10.8% in the EU.
- World Bank representative Millard F. Long signed a $60 million loan agreement yesterday with Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy and Antal Tombor, CEO of the Hungarian Electricity Works (MVM).

- The losing consortium in the recent television broadcasting concession tender, has released a statement saying it is highly likely that the assessment of the tender does not meet the regulations laid down in the media law.
- Citibank has decided not to bid for a majority stake in Mezobank Rt.
- The State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) transferred the Ft 5.28 billion due to the chemical giant TVK from the privatization price.
- The Russian oil and gas giant Gazprom has acquired minority stakes in the regional gas suppliers Egaz and Degaz, through offshore companies.
- Albert Szabo, Hungary's leading neo-Nazi, was yesterday given a suspended sentence of one year in prison for incitement against a community.
- A tornado touched down in Edeleny, northeast Hungary yesterday, damaging the roofs of about 30 houses and ripping most of the tiles off the local reformed church.
- Two gunmen stole Ft 1 million yesterday afternoon from the Afrika Tours travel agency, on Raday utca, in Budapest's ninth district.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Parliament may this summer see the report of its committee looking into the much-debated credit, debtor and bank consolidation scheme that cost the state about Ft 400 billion between 1992 and 1995, committee chairman Mihaly Varga said.
- The Interior Ministry has requested nearly 10 billion forints up to 1999 to handle election costs.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The Agriculture Ministry will receive direct subsidies of Ft 110 billion in 1998, and another Ft 8.3 billion from other revenues.
